newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bourse to move sideways before U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bourse to move sideways before U.S. data.

text.p: The Brussels blue-chip Bel-20 index closed up 0.13 percent at 2,106.98 points on Wednesday with dealers groping around for near-term direction.

Traders said all eyes were on Wall Street after recent volatility and on U.S. March jobs data, due on Friday, for fresh signs of inflationary pressures, which could trigger more U.S. interest rate hikes.

"We don't have many more publications of company results in Belgium to give the market direction, so the market will be very sensitive to Wall Street, U.S. interest rates and the dollar," one trader said.

Analysts were undecided about whether the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise interest rates again soon, but it was clear that players were cautious ahead of the next policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in May.
"It's fifty-fifty on whether the Fed raises rates. If it does, then it's the end of the bull run," another trader said.
"If rates rise again, it will be a signal for a severe correction on Wall Street and in Europe," a third said.
While others sat on their hands, awaiting news, some players were active on the bourse, picking up stocks which had suffered severe corrections, they added.
Attention centred on insurer Royale Belge, which closed up 3.33 percent at 8,700 francs.
Traders attributed the rise to investors betting on the share benefiting from a merger between RB's French parent UAP and rival AXA.
"The merger deal has played a part in today's rise," a trader said.
Internationally active shipper CMB fell a large 3.59 percent to 2,550 francs due to the weak dollar, traders said.
Among other dollar-sensitive stocks retailer Delhaize closed down 1.06 percent at 1,860 francs. In the same sector GIB ended down 1.26 percent at 1,570 francs.
